verdict.rationale: Notion documents several kinds of credential an agent could use, each with some scoping. Internal connections are limited to a single workspace and use a static token, personal access tokens act as one user, and public OAuth connections let you choose their installation scope. A connection also sees only the Custom Agents explicitly shared with it, and workspace owners can manage MCP client access. Missing for 10: documented capability-level scopes (e.g. read-only vs write permissions per token), explicit least-privilege guidance for agent credentials, and independent or hands-on corroboration of how granular the scoping really is.
